column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
A compass sits next to a wire. When the key is closed the needle swings. What do you conclude about the wire?
Who first noticed this effect of a current on a compass and what did it show?
Why do tiny pieces of iron sprinkled around a bar magnet form a pattern instead of staying scattered?
Outside a bar magnet, which pole do the lines leave from and where do they end, and what happens within it?
Where around a magnet would you find the lines packed most tightly, and what does that tell you? Why can two lines never meet?
What shape do iron filings make around a vertical wire carrying current, and what happens to the direction if you reverse the battery?
Predict what a compass needle would do if you doubled the current, and what it would do if you moved the compass further away.
A vertical wire carries current upwards. Describe how you would use your hand to work out which way the field circles around it.
Is there another everyday picture, with a screw, that gives the same direction as the thumb rule?
Describe the pattern of the field lines at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop and why every part of the loop helps.
How could you make the magnetic field at the centre of a loop ten times as strong without changing the current?
A long coil of wire carries a current. How would its outside field compare with a bar magnet's, and what is the field like inside?
Explain how you could turn an iron nail into a magnet that works only when you want it to.
A rod hanging between the poles of a strong magnet is pushed sideways as soon as a current flows through it. What does this tell you?
Which two things can you reverse to make the push on the rod change direction, and at what angle between current and field is the push strongest?
A current flows in a wire placed across the space between two magnet poles. How would you use the fingers of one hand to work out which way the wire is pushed?
Name some everyday devices that depend on a magnet pushing on a wire that carries current.
Which colours mark the two supply wires in a house, what voltage is between them, and how are the fan and bulb connected to them?
A faulty toaster's metal body becomes live. How does the earth wire stop you from getting a dangerous shock when you touch it?
List ways in which the current in a home circuit can suddenly become dangerously high.
Explain how a thin wire in a cartridge can save an appliance from being destroyed when too much current flows.
